name: mem
description: Low-level memory allocation and manipulation.  SAFETY: These are unsafe operations with no bounds checking. Improper use can cause segmentation faults and memory corruption.  Allocation failure is reported as ErrAlloc, so a program with something useful to do when memory runs out can handle it like any other error. The standard library does not: its own allocation sites use `!`, which aborts with a message naming the allocation. See specification 11.1 -- a library function has no way to report the failure that would not make every one of its callers fallible for a condition none of them can act on. doccheck: page-context doccheck: page-setup 1024 mem::alloc! -> buf doccheck: page-setup 1024 mem::alloc! -> dst doccheck: page-setup 1024 mem::alloc! -> src doccheck: page-setup 1024 mem::alloc! -> other_buf doccheck: page-setup 0 -> idx doccheck: page-setup 4 -> len doccheck: page-setup 42 -> elem

constants.name: AnySize
constants.description: Size in bytes of one `set_any`/`get_any` slot: eight bytes of value and eight of type tag. A container over a type parameter sizes its storage with this rather than with `sizeof<T>`, since one body has to hold every T.

functions.description: Allocate aligned memory. The returned pointer is aligned to the specified boundary. Use standard mem::free to deallocate.

params.name: alignment

functions.name: set_any
functions.description: Store a value of any type, with its type, in the slot at offset.  The slot takes over the reference the value came with, and gives it back when the slot is overwritten or cleared, so a string or a struct kept in one stays alive as long as the slot does. The region must be zeroed before first use -- `mem::zero` does it, and a zeroed slot reads back as the integer 0.

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset from base, a multiple of AnySize
